title: 48-year-old woman with abdominal pain
arrival: A 48-year-old woman presents with mild, generalised abdominal pain that began this morning.
feedbackWhy: This patient does not meet any red or yellow criteria. However, her temperature is above the high-risk threshold of 39°C. She should not be moved directly to the low-acuity or waiting area without immediate review by a supervising clinician.
reviewNote: This case's source-defined outcome is “Up-triage / immediate review by a supervising clinician,” distinct from a plain Yellow or Green. Confirm the scoring convention used for this against learner answers of Yellow or Green (currently: Green = under-triage, Yellow/Red = over-triage).

airway_red.text: No stridor. No respiratory distress. No central cyanosis.

circulation_red.text: Peripheral pulse strong. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding.

disability_red.text: No convulsions. Alert with normal mental status.

other_red.text: Age 48. Not pregnant. Mild, generalised abdominal pain that began this morning. No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb or chest pain. Not aggressive.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: Mild nausea only. No vomiting. Drinking normally. No diarrhoea, bleeding or fainting.

disability_yellow.text: Alert and calm. Walking independently. Pain 4 out of 10.

other_yellow.text: Abdomen is soft, with no guarding. No urinary retention. No rash, deformity, fracture, dislocation or surgical diagnosis.

exampleShows: No red or yellow criterion is met.
Her temperature of 39.4°C is above the 39°C high-risk threshold, so she needs immediate review by a supervising clinician rather than going straight to the waiting area.
